label: copy-phase echo of f early in the copy (recall_idx 1-3)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the fed-back input is the letter f (100% of mass), and almost only at recall_idx 1-3 (i.e. f was original token 0-2; recall_idx 2 = 58% of mass, 1 = 34%). Never fires in the original or delimiter phase, or on any other input token. Within this context it fires on only ~7% of eligible steps (precision 0.07 at recall ~1.0): it is sparser in short sequences (stronger for L=8-9, many outputs still to go) and stronger when the upcoming outputs include certain tokens (out_tok f/m/1/x/z, next_out q; top examples often have q a couple of positions after f). Those content conditions raise precision to ~0.25 but drop recall to ~0.55, so the gating on later sequence content was not captured cleanly. Magnitude is largest when f is original token 1 and the sequence is long.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=2 & in_tok=f (+6.23), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=f (+5.29), recall_idx=3 & in_tok=f (+3.55), phase=2 & out_tok=f (+3.54), phase=2 & in_tok=f (+3.24), phase=2 & out_tok=1 (+2.98). Lower it: correct=1 (-5.54), orig2=2 (-2.43), out_tok=y (-2.40), next_out=- (-2.22).
